issues.what: The reported headline ('pre-registered null rejected on 1 min, all 7 tests, MEAN-REVERTING: session memory beyond the hour effect; excess_beyond_hour_effect_inr +53..+106') is a false positive of a mis-specified null. N1 permutes outcomes within session x hour_bin cells over FIXED positions, but the positions are generated by the outcomes: a Foundation trade runs until exit and the next SETUP follows it (gap >= 1 bar everywhere), and winners hold ~6x longer than losers, so in a multi-unit cell the early units are losers almost by construction. A memoryless process reproduces the rejection and its direction exactly. The 'no key / null_result' conclusion is not refuted (it is strengthened); the memory claim, the 'direction' and the 'reverse rule' follow-up are.
issues.where: studies/session_stop/session_stop.py null_test() lines 135-155 and docstring lines 25-27 ('positions fixed ... so a rejection is session memory beyond the hour effect'); FINDINGS.md section 0 (line 7), section 3 'Reading' (line 82: 'there is session memory beyond the hour effect'), section 6 (line 308 'reverse rule'); findings.json keys session_memory_null_rejected / direction; the study agent's summary fields direction, excess_beyond_hour_effect_inr, null_N1.rejected
issues.evidence: Reproduced from data/minute (scratchpad refute_session_stop.py, IS rows only): L1 winners hold 110.6 bars vs losers 18.7 (stop exits 8.2); of the 3,222 units in multi-unit session x hour cells the non-last unit wins 1.5% vs the last 23.1%; P(another SETUP follows in the session | win) 0.571 vs 0.925 for a loss. My own zero-memory generator (outcome drawn iid from the hour_bin pool of real IS units, the drawn unit's duration, empirical gaps, real session skeleton with 15:25 cut): N1 (400 draws) rejected on 4/4 streams with threshold excess +76..+111 INR and Spearman excess -0.0215 -- the numbers the study reports as memory (+53..+106, -0.0233); with the duration drawn independently of the outcome 0/4 streams reject (excess +3..+26). The study's own repair agrees: results_repair.json timeframes.minute.n1_demonstration tied-duration streams n1_rejected_share 1.0 (min Holm p median 0.007, excess +84..+119, Spearman -0.0236) vs 0.06 for independent duration; hindsight-free re-tests N3 (2,000 memoryless streams) and N4 (within-hour contrast across sessions, session-block bootstrap) give min Holm p 1.0000 on minute L1 and on L0 (repair_null_tests_minute_L1.csv, _L0.csv; log line 34 'NOT REJECTED under N3 or N4 -> no session memory shown').
issues.fix: Withdraw the memory / direction / reverse-rule statements and the N1 excess numbers from every summary, REPORT.md and the S49 entry; state 'no session memory shown beyond the hour effect (N3/N4 min Holm p 1.0); the as-run N1 rejection is an artifact of outcome-dependent trade duration'. issues.what: FINDINGS section 4 uses the session-matched random-control percentile (0.0 for all 32 cells) as the decisive evidence ('the rule does worse than picking the same number of same-session SETUPs at random in essentially every draw'). For an absorbing within-session rule that keeps the earliest positions, this control is a hindsight-biased comparator: the number of positions n_s is known only at session end and the last positions of a session are the long winners by construction, so a zero-memory book gets the same 0.0th percentile. The 'no edge' conclusion survives on the other checks, but this sentence and the go_no_go control_pct check are not evidence.
